summary: Mircea Eliade was a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bucharest under Nae Ionescu, studied at the University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, and held professorships at the Sorbonne and the University of Chicago.
Mireille Helffer was a scholar in Tibetology. She served as a Chargé de Recherche at CNRS from circa 1964 to 1993, with an affiliation at Paris Nanterre University attested in 1985.

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD from the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, later holding posts at the University of New South Wales and the University of Western Australia.

Miriam Levering was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She received her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška studied at the University of Zagreb, the University of Ljubljana (PhD), and the International Faculty of Comparative Law. He held academic posts at the University of Zagreb, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale Law School from circa 1976 to 2023.

Mirle Srinivasa Nagaraja Rao was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at the University of Mysore and Savitribai Phule Pune University. His career included serving at Karnatak University, Karnataka's archaeology department, and as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1984–1987).
Mitchell G. Weiss is a scholar of Indology who studied under Ludo Rocher. He has held a post as Professor at the University of Basel.

Mitsuji Fukunaga worked in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies, having studied at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. He held professorships at Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.

Mitsukuni Yoshida was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1942 to 1945 and later held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts from circa 1980 to 1986.
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and served there as a lecturer, attested between 1989 and 1995.

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned doctorates from the University of Munich and Kokugakuin University, later serving as professor at Kokugakuin, Nihon University, and the University of Tsukuba, and head of the Eastern Institute.

Mitsuyuki Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1932 to 1935 and later served as a professor at Ryukoku University (circa 1951–1976) and International Buddhist University (circa 1976–1982).
Miyoko Nakano is a Sinologist who studied at Hokkaido University from circa 1952 to 1956. She subsequently held an academic post at Hokkaido University from circa 1971 to 1996.

Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Tokai University and Gakushuin University under Atsuhiko Yoshida and Katsuhiko Kamimura, later holding a teaching post at Meisei University attested in 2008.
Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held a post as professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.
Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned an MPhil and served as a research scholar at Vikram University, both attested in 2014.

Mohammad Habib was a historian and archaeologist. He completed his education at the University of Allahabad (circa 1911–1915), Aligarh Muslim University (circa 1916–1919), and New College, Oxford (circa 1919–1922).

Mokurai Shimaji was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Chō Sanshū. He held leadership posts at Nishi Hongan-ji, Hongan-ji, and Gankyo-ji, and founded Chiyoda Jogakuen in 1888.

Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin in 2001. In 2006, she was attested as a research fellow at the University of Berlin and a part-time teacher at Heidelberg.

Monica Esposito was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Paris Diderot University/University of Paris, completed postdoctoral studies in Venice, Paris, and Kansai University, and was an Associate Professor at Kyoto University in 2003.
